author: WP19
summary: Alpha.1-era chapter on proving engagement on hostile hosts: Wine wrapper gates, the discovery bypass, Proton lanes, virtual displays and browser verdicts. The Direct3D gate table was already on the WP09 Direct3D evidence page; the Direct2D prefix/Proton/display machinery, the discovery hatch (whose reach is wider than the chapter says), the browser verdict mechanics and the two-verdict model are new on the oracles deep dive. Wrappers and workarounds of retired renderer generations were dropped.

concepts.text: Some hosts return success while substituting a different runtime (Wine falling back from DXVK, an unpinned Proton, a browser page that never reaches a frame, discovery that opens no device); there the first oracle is proof that the intended execution route engaged.
tokens: the first oracle is not the game's output

concepts.section: The Wine wrapper as a verdict pipeline
concepts.text: The Wine wrappers validate arguments, choose an isolated prefix, set diagnostics, refuse a missing prefix with setup instructions instead of bootstrapping it, run wine through tee, preserve Wine's exit status and only then inspect the captured log.

target.evidence: scripts/run-wine-dxvk9.sh; scripts/run-wine-dxvk.sh; scripts/run-wine-vkd3d.sh (system.reg check, tee, PIPESTATUS)

concepts.section: The Wine wrapper as a verdict pipeline
concepts.text: The DIRECTX9 and DIRECTX11 wrappers require a DXVK: <version> log line and the DIRECTX12 wrapper a vkd3d-proton applicationVersion line; without it the wrapper exits 3 regardless of the program's own status, so a pass through the wrong translation layer is a failed experiment.

concepts.section: The Wine wrapper as a verdict pipeline
concepts.text: The unit's marker list also covers wrappers for older Direct3D and DirectDraw generations; those renderer families were retired and their wrappers removed.
concepts.note: Retired renderer families (Bible ch71 Wine-wrapper section); no wrapper for them exists in scripts/ at TARGET. Names withheld by policy.

concepts.section: The Wine wrapper as a verdict pipeline
concepts.text: Prefix map as reproducibility: DIRECTX9 and DIRECTX11 share ~/.wine-cna-d3d11 through separate variables and DIRECTX12 uses its own prefix; the per-generation prefixes and host workarounds (a forced host display, a forced software driver) belonged to retired families.

concepts.section: The Wine wrapper as a verdict pipeline
concepts.text: Direct2D is the exception: its Wine launcher defaults to the ordinary $HOME/.wine without mutating it, and a separate suite creates a fresh prefix in a temporary directory with only wineboot --init; reproducible evidence should prefer the disposable route and record the prefix identity.
tokens: defaults to the developer's ordinary $HOME/.wine prefix
concepts.note: Known Issues B6 classified the default prefix as a design decision (CNA-BUG-034 NOT A BUG).

concepts.section: Discovery needs a controlled escape hatch
concepts.text: Cross-compiled CnaTests uses CROSSCOMPILING_EMULATOR to put the Wine wrapper before the executable; discovery runs --gtest_list_tests, which creates no device, so per-wrapper CNA_*_SKIP_*_GATE=1 variables in the emulator command bypass the engagement check, and writing the bypass into the generated command keeps it reviewable.

concepts.section: Discovery needs a controlled escape hatch
concepts.text: Claim that execution CTests run with the gate enabled: at TARGET the emulator is a target property, so every discovered CnaTests case and every CnaTests-command route also runs through the gate-free wrapper; translation-layer engagement is proved only by separately registered renderer programs, which keep the gate unless they never open a device.
tokens: Its reach is wider than discovery

concepts.section: Proton solves a different reproducibility problem
concepts.text: The Direct2D Proton runner pins its runtime through a checked-in priority list (Proton 9.0 Beta, then Proton 8.0), refuses Experimental unless an explicit override marks the run non-reproducible, and publishes the runtime identity including the DXVK version read from the shipped DLL.

concepts.section: Proton solves a different reproducibility problem
concepts.text: Both Proton runners refuse to operate on the ordinary Wine prefix, a safeguard added after a recorded incident in which a Proton wine call without an explicit prefix half-upgraded a developer's personal prefix and hung for hours.
tokens: Both Proton runners refuse the ordinary

concepts.section: Proton solves a different reproducibility problem
concepts.text: Neither Proton path applies the log-token gate: Direct2D combines exit status with its published pinned identity, while the DIRECTX12 lane defaults to the moving Experimental install, overlays two vkd3d-proton DLLs, forwards only the child's exit status and needs file-based diagnostics, so a pass there is route evidence with weaker reproducibility.
tokens: forwards only the child's exit status

concepts.section: Proton solves a different reproducibility problem
concepts.text: Engagement proof must match the host's actual substitution risk rather than be copied mechanically from one wrapper to the next.
tokens: engagement proof has to match the host's actual substitution risk

target.evidence: framing drawn from the two Proton lanes

concepts.section: Virtual displays are infrastructure, not evidence
concepts.text: The Direct2D virtual-display wrapper validates the Xvfb geometry, keeps X authority in a temporary directory, installs cleanup traps and is reentrant, which makes headless presentation repeatable.

concepts.section: Virtual displays are infrastructure, not evidence
concepts.text: A virtual display does not prove physical display behaviour, vendor drivers, HDR or composition, and a Windows executable exiting zero under Wine is not a native-Windows result; the claim must carry compiler, executable format, Wine or Proton version, translation backend, device, display server and prefix.
tokens: does not become a native-Windows result

concepts.text: A WebAssembly exit status is not observable, so the HTML_DOM and SVG_DOM pages publish completion and result fields on window; the Playwright driver waits with a bounded timeout, fails on page exceptions and [FAIL] console lines, and combines that verdict with structural and screenshot evidence.
tokens: treats a page exception or a [FAIL] console line as a failure

concepts.text: Serving over loopback HTTP is part of the environment: the wrappers start a local server, poll it for readiness and kill it from a cleanup trap, never use file://, and give the six HTML_DOM pages distinct ports so concurrent runs cannot collide.

The compositor check decodes a browser screenshot into a canvas and samples pixels with a bounded RGB tolerance, and SVG_DOM adds namespace and hidden-canvas assertions to prove the SVG implementation, not a look-alike image, supplied the frame.

concepts.section: Hostility is any plausible false green
concepts.text: Wine fallback, stale Proton selection, headless skips, browser startup without a frame and renderer impersonation share one failure mode; a robust harness gives an engagement verdict and a behaviour verdict and passes only on both, making evidence of non-substitution a first-class artifact.
tokens: make evidence of non-substitution a first-class artifact

target.evidence: framing; DirectX11_DxvkGate as the CNA instance of a tested engagement gate

issues.text: In cross-compiled DIRECTX9/11/12 and Direct2D trees, CnaTests runs through a gate-free Wine wrapper for discovery and for every discovered case, so device-creating GoogleTest cases are not proven to have run through DXVK/vkd3d-proton.
The DIRECTX12 Proton lane uses the moving Proton Experimental runtime, has no pin or identity record and no log-token gate.
run-wine-direct2d.sh defaults to $HOME/.wine by design and performs no prefix mutation.
